why: A (lemma_7_10) takes the natural action as a project NaturalRep, whose domain V(x) = R.U must be CONNECTED; B takes Theorem 7.1's clauses as data on any open V(x) (IsNatActionB, no connectedness). For connected V(x) B's data is a NaturalRep (Phi(1) = id and Phi(g)^-1 = Phi(g^-1) follow from Phi_mul) and A gives B: proved as A_to_B_of_isConnected; for disconnected V(x) A says nothing, and B (true, the averaging proof needs no connectedness) would have to be re-proved. Conversely A drops the hypothesis x in U(x) and adds the conclusion tsupport f in cl U(x); B gives only tsupport f in V(x) and needs x in U(x), so B does not yield A (e.g. for x in cl U(x) minus U(x)). Both differences are genuine statement differences, not proof effort.
